                     </ns0:gap>y the Spirit of God. <ns0:hi>He heareth the Word.</ns0:hi> He (saith the Apostle) who is born of God heareth us; Faith cometh by hearing And <ns0:hi>understand<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth it. Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Receiveth it,</ns0:hi> that is, not in the meer No<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, but by Faith, and a mind willing to learn, and be instru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cted, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> adds, and <ns0:hi>keepeth it,</ns0:hi> retains the Savour and Impres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion of it upon his Soul. <ns0:hi>W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ich also beareth Fruit,</ns0:hi> the Fruit of holiness, in his Life, in an obedience to the Will of God, for all <ns0:hi>Seed</ns0:hi> bringeth forth Fruit, according to his kind. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> adds, with <ns0:hi>Patience,</ns0:hi> by which is to be under<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tood <ns0:hi>Cer<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, Constancy,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Perseverance,</ns0:hi> and that notwithstanding all Tryals and opposit<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ons he meets with from the World, the Flesh and the Devil. <ns0:hi>Some an hundred Fold,</ns0:hi> some <ns0:hi>Sixty,</ns0:hi> some <ns0:hi>T<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>irty,</ns0:hi> not all alike. A Soul may be an hone<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, and good Soul, and that (as we see here) in Christs opinion and <ns0:hi>Iudgment,</ns0:hi> tho it doth not bring forth Fruit in the same Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />portion with others.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:242" />24 Another parable he put forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man, which sowed good seed in his field.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 But while men slept, his enemy came, and sowed tares amongst the wheat, and went a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />way.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 So the servants of the housholder came, and said unto him, Sir, didst thou not sow good seed in thy field, from whence then hath it tares?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants then said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go, and gather them up?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 But he said, Nay, lest while ye gather up the ta<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>es, ye root up also the wheat with them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 Let both grow together until the harvest, and in the time of harvest, I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them, but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.12.</ns0:note> gather the wheat into my barn.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 4.30.31. Luke 13.19.</ns0:note> The kingdom of heaven is like unto a grain of mustard-seed, which a man took and sow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in his field.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">
                  <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See the Expli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation of these in the Notes to</ns0:hi> v. 43.</ns0:note>32 Which indeed is the least of all seeds, but when it is grown, it is the greatest amongst herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air, come and lodge in the branches there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />of.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 13.20.</ns0:note> Another parable spake he unto them, The kingdom of heaven, is like unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>A Measure <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ting a pin<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> of a Peck and a half.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.<ns0:note place="bottom">Here are three Parables by the Evangelist put together before he cometh to the <ns0:hi>Explication,</ns0:hi> which our Saviour gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veth of the first. All of them concerning the Gospel Church, and the Dispensation of the Gospel. In the one he instructs us what we are to expect as to the mixture of Persons in it, while it is in this World. In the other two concerning the Increase and Propagation of it. The first himself Expound<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43. This Parable is only found in <ns0:hi>Matthew.</ns0:hi> The other two are found, shortly both of them in <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> one in <ns0:hi>Mark,</ns0:hi> neither of them are Expoun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded. I will therefore without any Explication of these Verses at present, go on to the Verses following them, all which will lead me to our Saviours own interpretation of the first of these Parables, after which I will also consider those two Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rables that follow here, but are neither Expounded here, nor in the other Evangelists.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 4.33.</ns0:note> All these things spake Jesus unto the multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude in parables, and without a parable sp<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ke he not unto them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables, I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.<ns0:note place="bottom">Christ spake all the afore mentioned things to the Multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude, and also to his Disciples in <ns0:hi>Parables,</ns0:hi> dark sayings, co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vering Divine, and Spiritual Truths, with fit, and proper Si<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />militudes, and at this time he delivered himself wholly in this manner to them, tho at other times he spake more plainly. He gave us the reason before, and by this way of speaking, al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so he made his own Disciples more diligent to attend to what they heard, and more inqu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tive after the true sense and mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of it. And thus saith the Evangeli<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, that which was spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken by the <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>het, Psa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi> 78.2. was also fulfilled in Christ, not that the Psalmist, <ns0:hi>whether David</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Asaph,</ns0:hi> did there Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecy concerning Christ, for plainly the Psalmist intended to relate the History of Gods dealing with the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> and their behaviour toward him. Nor was it fulfilled, as the Type in the <ns0:hi>Antitype,</ns0:hi> but as a thing of the same Nature was done; the <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> delivered himself in <ns0:hi>dark Sayings,</ns0:hi> so did Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, but instead of <ns0:hi>I will utter dark sayings of old,</ns0:hi> the Evangelist hath, <ns0:hi>which have been kept secret, from the Foundation of the World,</ns0:hi> he means the great, and Mysterious things of the Gospel, <ns0:hi>hid</ns0:hi> from <ns0:hi>Ages</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Generations, Rom.</ns0:hi> 16.25. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.7. <ns0:hi>Colos.</ns0:hi> 1.26. where it is called the <ns0:hi>Revelation of the Mystery, which was kept secret since the World began, Eph<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi> 3.9. As the Psalmist opened his Mouth in Grave Discourses, tending to the good of the People, to whom he spake: So Christ taught the People, by revealing the Mysteries of the Gospel, <ns0:hi>hid in God from the beginning of the World,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> speaks to the <ns0:hi>Ephesians.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 Then Jesus sent the multitude away, and went into the house, and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Multitude went away, (as most People do from Sermons) never the wiser, understanding nothing of what they heard, nor caring to understand it. But there was a more Conscientious part of our Saviours Auditory, who could not thus satisfy themseves, they follow Christ into the house, and intreat him to open to them the <ns0:hi>Parable of the Tares of the Field,</ns0:hi> they say nothing of the other two <ns0:hi>Parables,</ns0:hi> because probably they understood them, and it may be this Parable did more affect them, in regard of the dreadful Conclusion of it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 He answered and said unto them, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 The field is the world, the good seed are the children of the kingdom, but the tares are <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 3.15. Acts 13.10. 1 Joh. 3.8.</ns0:note> the children of the wicked one.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 The enemy that sowed them is the devil, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joel 3.13. Rev. 14.15.</ns0:note> the harvest is the end of the world, and the rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pers are the angels.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Design that Christ had in this Parable, was to shew them, that though he laid a good Foundation of a Church in the World, calling some home to himself, and making t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>em partakers of his effectual Grace, laying the Foundation of his Gospel Church, in such as took his Yoke upon them, yet in process of time, whiles those that should succeed him in his Ministry slept, (not bei<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>g so diligent and watchful as they ought to be) the Devil (who is full of Envy and Malice to mens Souls, and is continually going about, seeking whom he might devour) would sow Erroneous opinions, and find a party even in the Bosome of his Church, who would hear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken to him, and through their Lusts comply with his Temp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tations, both to Errors in Doctrine, and Errors in Practice; and it was his Will, that there should be in the Visible Church, a mixture of good and bad, such bad ones especially, as Men could not purge out without a danger of putting out such as were true and sincere, but there would be a time<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> in the End of the World, when he would come with his Fan, and throughly purge his Floor, a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>d take to Heaven all true and sincere Souls, but turn all Hypocrites into Hell. This appears by our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour's Exposition, to have been our Saviours plain meaning in this Parable. Hence he tells us, That by the <ns0:hi>Sower</ns0:hi> here, he meant himself <ns0:hi>the Son of Man.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>the</ns0:hi> Field, he <ns0:hi>meant the World.</ns0:hi> By the good Seed, he meant the <ns0:hi>Children of the Kingdom.</ns0:hi> Such as had a true Change wrought in their Hearts, were truly Regenerated, and Converted. By the <ns0:hi>Tares</ns0:hi> he meant the <ns0:hi>Children of the Wicked one,</ns0:hi> that is, of the Devil. Such as did the Works of the Devil, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 8.44. That the Enemy that sowed these Tares, was the Devil, who by his Sugge<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tions, presenting objects, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> makes himself the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> of all wicked Men. Our Saviour here saith nothing to that part of the Parable, where the <ns0:hi>Tares</ns0:hi> are said to be sown (<ns0:hi>W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ile Men slept</ns0:hi>) That was plain and intelligible <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nough. The Devil hath a Power to <ns0:hi>Seduce, Persuade</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lure,</ns0:hi> none to force. If particular Persons kept their Watch, as they might, the Devil could not by his Temptation force them. If <ns0:hi>Magistrates</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ministers</ns0:hi> kept their Watches ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to Gods Prescripti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, there could not be so much open Wickedness in the World, as there is. Neither doth our Saviour give us any particular <ns0:hi>Explication</ns0:hi> of that part of the <ns0:hi>Parable,</ns0:hi> which is <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28, 29. where the Servants say to their Master, <ns0:hi>Wilt thou then that we go, and gather them up. And he said unto them, Nay, lest while you ga<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther up the Tares, you root up also-the W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>eat with them.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour by this teacheth us<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that every passage in a para<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, is not to be <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>itted by something in the <ns0:hi>Explication</ns0:hi>; It was not the Point that he designed in this Parable to instruct them in, how far Church-O<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ficers might or ought to act in purging the Church. But only that in the <ns0:hi>Visible Church,</ns0:hi> they must expect a <ns0:hi>Mixture,</ns0:hi> till the Day of Judgment, 2. That in that Day he would make a perfect Separation. So as <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>hose that would from this pa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sage in the Parable conclude. That all Erroneous, and loose Persons, o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ght to be Tole<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rated in the Church, till the Day of Judg<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ent, forget the Common Rule in Divinity, that <ns0:hi>Parabolical Divinit<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> is not Argumentative.</ns0:hi> We can argue from nothing in a Parable, but from the main <ns0:hi>Scope</ns0:hi> and Tendency of it. However it is bold Arguing from a pas<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>age in a Parable, Expounded by our Saviour himself, when he hath omitted the Exp<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ication of that passage, Nor can any thing be concluded<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t that such must not be Rooted out, as have such a Resemblance of <ns0:hi>W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>eat</ns0:hi> from the outwar<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> appearance, that they cannot be Rooted out, without a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Hazard of a mistake, and a Rooting up of the Wheat with them, but our Saviour reserves the point of t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e Ministerial Duty in purging the Curch, to another more proper ti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e, he here saith nothing of that, but of his own De<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ign to purge it <ns0:hi>at the Harvest.</ns0:hi> Which he interprets, the <ns0:hi>End of the World,</ns0:hi> that is, the <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> of Iudgment.</ns0:hi> By the <ns0:hi>Reap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ers,</ns0:hi> he tells us that he meaneth the <ns0:hi>Angels.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:243" />40 As therefore the tares are gathered, and burnt in the fire, so shall it be in the end of this world.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Scandals, Stumbling blocks.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> things that offend, and them that do iniquity.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.12.</ns0:note> there shall be wailing, and gnashing of teeth.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 15.42.</ns0:note> Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Vers.</ns0:hi> 9.</ns0:note> Who hath ears to hear, let <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>im hear.<ns0:note place="bottom">As in the Common practice of M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n, when they have a mind to pick their Corn, and have it clean, when it is Reap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, to set Men to Clean the Wheat, and to pick out the Tares, and having tyed them up in Bundles, to burn them, so (saith he) I will do. I will send my <ns0:hi>Ange<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s</ns0:hi> at the Day of Judgment, and they shall out of my Church, take all im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />penitent Sinners, all those who in this World have been <ns0:hi>Scan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dals,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Offences,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mischievous</ns0:hi> to my People, and who have made it their business to work Iniquity. <ns0:hi>And they shall cast them into a Furnace of Fire, where shall be wail<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing and Gnashing of Teeth.</ns0:hi> That is into Hell, which in re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gard of the severe Torments<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which the Damned shall feel there, is often in Scripture compared to Fire, as <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 25.41. and in other Texts, by which is only set out to us, the dread<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fulness of the Punishment of the Damned, that is Proporti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />oned to, if not far exceeding that of the burning living Bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dies in fire. Having thus expressed the punishment of Wick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed Men, he Expoundeth what he means by <ns0:hi>gathering the Wheat into his Barn,</ns0:hi> viz. The taking of Righteous Men to Heaven. <ns0:hi>Then</ns0:hi> saith he, <ns0:hi>shall the Righteous,</ns0:hi> those whom I have Clothed with my Righteousness, and who have lived in obedience to my Will to that degree, that tho they be not perfectly <ns0:hi>Righteous,</ns0:hi> yet are sincere and upright, so as I have accepted them. <ns0:hi>Shine as the Sun</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of their Father,</ns0:hi> an Expression much like that of <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 12.2.3. Significative of that Glorious State of the Saints in Heaven, which no Eye having seen, nor Ear having heard, no Tongue is able to Express. He concludeth in the same man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner, as he concludeth the Parable of the <ns0:hi>Sower,</ns0:hi> exciting his Hearers to a diligent Consideration, and Belief of what he had said. Our Saviour adding no particular <ns0:hi>Explication</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>two Parable<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> delivered <ns0:hi>v,</ns0:hi> 31, 32, 33. the Disciples not ask<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing him to explain them, and the Evangelist having put the <ns0:hi>Explication</ns0:hi> of the first <ns0:hi>Parable</ns0:hi> after them. It is reasonable, that tho I omitted the Explication of them in their proper place, yet I should add something here for the Benefit of those, who possibly will not be able so readily, to conceive our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viours meaning in them, without an Interpreter, as the Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples did, which is thought to be the reason, why they ask<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed no Explication of them. The one is the <ns0:hi>Parable</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Grain of Mustard Seed, v.</ns0:hi> 31, 32. The other, the <ns0:hi>Para<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Leaven</ns0:hi> hid in <ns0:hi>three Measures of Meal, v.</ns0:hi> 33. The Scope of both is the same. Our Saviour intended them both, to let his Disciples know the Success, that his Gospel should have over all the World, that they might not be dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />couraged at the little Success of it at present. To this pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose he compareth it. First, to a <ns0:hi>Grain of Mustard Seed,</ns0:hi> which he saith, is the <ns0:hi>least of all Seeds,</ns0:hi> that is one of the least of Seeds, or the least Seed, that produceth so great a Plant, but <ns0:hi>becomes a Tree so high, that the Birds of the Air, come and Lodg in the Branches of it.</ns0:hi> Tho that <ns0:hi>small Seed</ns0:hi> with us, runs up to a great heigth, and produceth a Plant which hath Branches considerable enough to Lodg Birds, which sit low, yet we must not Judge of what grew in those Countries, by what groweth in ours, there are strange, and almost incredible Stories, told of that Plant by Naturalists, as to its growth in some hot, and fertile Countries. Christ by this foretold his Disciples, what following Ages quickly veri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fyed, That the Heathen should entertain the Gospel, and <ns0:hi>the sound of it should go to the Ends of the Earth.</ns0:hi> Notwith<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />standing its present small appearance. Upon the same Score he <ns0:hi>compareth</ns0:hi> it to a little <ns0:hi>Leaven, which a Woman hid in three Measures of Meal, till the whole Mass</ns0:hi> of Meal <ns0:hi>was leavened.</ns0:hi> By these two Expressions, our Saviour also lets us know, the <ns0:hi>quick</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>powerful</ns0:hi> Nature of the Word. That Christs words are (as he said) <ns0:hi>Spirit of Life,</ns0:hi> and have an hidden and extraordinary Virtue in them. I do not think it worth the while to inquire into the content of these <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> or Mea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sures of Meal, and why he mentioneth but three<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> They are Curiosities, the knowledge of which turneth to no account. Our Saviour certainly by the Expression, designed only to hint the <ns0:hi>small number</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> that believed in him, but fore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />told a far greater Harvest. <ns0:hi>The Law should go forth out of Sion, and the Word of the Lord from Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> Prophesied, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 2.3. But <ns0:hi>many People</ns0:hi> (after them) should say, <ns0:hi>Com you, let us go up to the Mountain of the house of the Lord.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 Again the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure, hid in a field, the which when a man hath found he hideth, and for joy thereof, go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Phil. 3.7, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.<ns0:note place="bottom">Whatsoever belongeth to the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of God,</ns0:hi> whether the <ns0:hi>Word,</ns0:hi> which is called the <ns0:hi>Word of the Kingdom,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Grace</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Favour of God,</ns0:hi> which he by me di<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>penseth out under the Administration of the Gospel, <ns0:hi>is like,</ns0:hi> that is, should be adjudged, e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>teemed, and used like as <ns0:hi>Treasure hidden in a Fie<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>d.</ns0:hi> Men should do by it, as they would do upon the Discovery of a great Sum of Money, buried up in the Earth, in some Field, not yet their own. Suppose a Man had made some such discovery, what would he do? he would rejoyce at it<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> he would hide it, he would sell all he had, and buy that Field, so should men do to whom there is a <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi> of the Gos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel, and the <ns0:hi>Grace thereof.</ns0:hi> They should inwardly rejoyce, in the Revelation, and bless God <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or it, and what ever it co<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t them, labour that they might be made partakers of that Grace. Earthly Possessions cannot be had without purcha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing, and those who have not ready Money to purchase with, must raise it from the Sale of something which they have, therefore our labour, for the Kingdom of Heaven is set out under the Notion of buying. But the Prophet <ns0:hi>Is.</ns0:hi> 55.1.2. lets us know that it is a <ns0:hi>buying without Money, and without Price,</ns0:hi> however there is some Resemblance, for as in <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>uying and selling, there is a parting with something that is ours, in Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />change for something which is anothers, so in order to the ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />taining of the Grace of the Gospel, and the Kingdom of Glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry, to which the Remission of Sins leadeth, we must part with something, in order to the obtaining of it. We have no rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy Money, nothing by us, that is, a <ns0:hi>Quid pro quo,</ns0:hi> a valuable Price for Divine Grace, we must therefore part with some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing that we have, and it is no matter, what it be, which God requireth. Where this Discovery is made, the Soul will part with all it hath, not only its old Heart, its unlawful De<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ires, and Lusts, but its Riches, Honours, Pleasures, if it can by no other means obtain the Kingdom of Heaven, that it may ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain it, they are all of no value to it. Nor is it at all necessa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry in order to <ns0:hi>buying,</ns0:hi> that the thing parted with, be of a proportionable value. Amongst Men, Wedges of Gold, have been purchased for Knives, and Rattles, <ns0:hi>&c</ns0:hi> nor doth any thing we can part with, that we may obtain the Kingdom of Heaven, bear any better Proportion, yet it is a buying, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause it is what God is pleased to accept, and upon the parting with, gives us this Heavenly Kingdom.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant-man, seeking goodly pearls.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 Who when he hath found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had and bought it.<ns0:note place="bottom">The State of the Gospel Dispensation, is such, that Men in it, having a Discovery of more excellent things, than before they were aware of, <ns0:hi>Life</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Immortality</ns0:hi> being <ns0:hi>brought to Light through the Gospel.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.10. <ns0:hi>Grace and Truth</ns0:hi> coming by <ns0:hi>Iesus Christ, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.17. Men and Women are set upon seeking for these Spiritual things, as Merchants do for goodly Pearls, and when God makes a Discovery of <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> and his Grace to the Soul, it appears to them as a <ns0:hi>Pearl</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>great Price,</ns0:hi> of more value than all they have in the World, and they are ready to part with all, to obtain Christ, and his Grace. Both these <ns0:hi>Parables</ns0:hi> have the same Scope, and Ten<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dency, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to inform us, that Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t and his Grace are of a great and Transcendent value. 2. That under the Gospel, there is a clear Discovery of these things to the World. 3. That where this Discovery is effectually, and particularly made to any Soul, that Soul will part with all it hat<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, or is worth, rather than it will miss of Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t and his Grace and Glory.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 Again the kingdom of heaven, is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />very kind.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 Which when it was full, they drew to shore
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:243" />
and sate down, and gathered the good into Vessels, but cast the bad away.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 So shall it be at the end of the world: The angels shall come forth, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 25.32.</ns0:note> sever the wicked from the just.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 And shall cast them into the furnace of fire, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Verse 42.</ns0:note> there shall be wailing, and gnashing of teeth.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Scope of this <ns0:hi>Parab<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e</ns0:hi> is much the same, with that of the <ns0:hi>Tares,</ns0:hi> to teach us that whil<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t the Church is in this World, there will be in it, a mixture of good, and bad, a perfect Se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />paration of which one from another, is not to be expected until the Day of Judgment. <ns0:hi>Again the Kingdom of Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven.</ns0:hi> This term signi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ieth the whole Dispensation, and Ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ministration of the Gospel, both the Grace Dispensed in it, and the means of that Grace, which is admini<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>red under it. I should here interpret it of the <ns0:hi>Preaching</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Gospel,</ns0:hi> which is called, the <ns0:hi>Word of the Kingdom</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> being the means by which Men are gathered in, both to the Church visible, and invi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ible. This our Lord here compareth to a <ns0:hi>Net,</ns0:hi> thrown into the <ns0:hi>Sea of the World,</ns0:hi> and gathering in of every kind, bringing in many to an outward Profe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sion, all of which shall not come to the Kingdom of Glory, nor are indeed true Members of Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, not Members of the Church invisible, tho they be Members of the Church visible. When the end of the World shall come, and Christ shall have ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />complished his Design in<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> the World, then a Day of Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment shall come, and there shall be a perfect <ns0:hi>Separation</ns0:hi> betwixt such as received the Gospel in Truth, and in the Love of it and others, the former shall be taken to Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, and the latter thrown into Hell; which he expresseth by the like Phrases, which he had before used in the Parable of the <ns0:hi>Tares,</ns0:hi> which need no further Explication.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 Jesus saith unto them. Have ye understood, all these things? They said unto him, Yea, Lord.<ns0:note place="bottom">A Conscientious Teacher, will have a respect to the profit of his Hearers. Christ here setteth us an Example, asking his Disciples, if they had understood <ns0:hi>all these things,</ns0:hi> as well those <ns0:hi>Parables</ns0:hi> of which he had given them, no parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cular Explication, as those he had explained. They say un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to him. <ns0:hi>Yea Lord,</ns0:hi> we have understood them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 Then said he unto them, Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven, is like unto a man, that is an housholder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new, and old.<ns0:note place="bottom">Seeing you understand these things, Communicate your knowledge of them unto others, do not know for your selves alone. <ns0:hi>Every Scribe that is instructed to the Kingdom of Heaven.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> were not only Clerks, that were imployed in Writing; but <ns0:hi>Teachers of the Law,</ns0:hi> such a one was <ns0:hi>Ezra ch.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6. Our Saviour here by <ns0:hi>Every Scribe instructed to the Kingdom of God,</ns0:hi> under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />standeth every <ns0:hi>good Minister of the Gospel,</ns0:hi> fitted to pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />move the Kingdom of God, to be imployed in the Church of God, should be <ns0:hi>like a good Housholder,</ns0:hi> that hath not his Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vision to seek, when his Guests come; but hath a full fraught Store-house, and hath nothing to do, but out of his <ns0:hi>Stock,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Store-house,</ns0:hi> to bring out all sort of Provision, accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to the various Pallats of his Guests: Ministers of the Gospel, should not be <ns0:hi>Novices,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 3.6. Raw, and Ig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />norant men, but Men mighty in the Scriptures, well ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quainted with the Writings of the Old, and New Testament, and the Sense of them, Men that have a stock of spiritual Know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge, able readily to speak, <ns0:hi>a Word to the Weary,</ns0:hi> and to speak to Men and Womens particular Cases, and Questions.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">53 And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="54">54 And when he was come into his <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 4.16.</ns0:note> own coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />try, he taught them in their synagogue, inso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />much that they were astonished, and said, whence hath this man wisdom, and <ns0:hi>these</ns0:hi> mighty works?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> relateth this Passage, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.1.2, 3, 4. Our Lord went up and down Preaching the Gospel, he having Preached unto the People in the former <ns0:hi>Parables,</ns0:hi> now he departeth from the <ns0:hi>Sea-side,</ns0:hi> where he Preached as before, <ns0:hi>into his own Countrey,</ns0:hi> most Interpreters judge <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> he was born in <ns0:hi>Bethlehem,</ns0:hi> but we read little or nothing of any time he spent there afterward. <ns0:hi>Nazareth</ns0:hi> was the place, where he was brought up, and therefore he was called <ns0:hi>Iesus of Nazareth.</ns0:hi> There he preached in the Synagogue, or in the Synagogues of <ns0:hi>Galilee. Mark</ns0:hi> addeth on the Sabbath Day. <ns0:hi>Insomuch that they were astonished.</ns0:hi> It is not said they repented, or be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved, but they admired at him, and were a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tonished, <ns0:hi>and said, whence hath this Man this Wisdom, and these mighty Works?</ns0:hi> That is, a Power to do these mighty Works. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>whence hath this Man these Things?</ns0:hi> And <ns0:hi>what Wisdom i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> this, that is given unto him, that even such mighty Works are wrought by his Hands?</ns0:hi> Astonishment, and Ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>iration flow from Ignorance, and are no Indications of any spiritual saving Work upon mens Hearts; we shall see that these <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> notwithstanding their <ns0:hi>Astonishment</ns0:hi>: are by and by scandalized, and offended at Christ.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="55">55 Is not this the carpenters son? <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 6.42.</ns0:note> Is not his mother called Mary, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 13.55.</ns0:note> and his brethren James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="56">56 And his sisters are they not all with us? Whence then, hath this man all these things?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.3. Only he saith: Is not this the <ns0:hi>Carpenter</ns0:hi>? <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which leadeth some to think, that Christ while he was thirty years of Age, wrought with <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> upon his Trade, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.51. it is said, <ns0:hi>That he came</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>was subject to his Parents. Ioseph</ns0:hi> was an Artificer, that was certain. So <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifies, but whe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther a <ns0:hi>Carpenter,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Smith,</ns0:hi> the word will not inform us; for the <ns0:hi>Brethren of Christ</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Sisters</ns0:hi> here mentioned, the mo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t by them under<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tand his near Relations. The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were offended at the meanness of our Saviour's <ns0:hi>Parents,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Relations. They were offended in him,</ns0:hi> that is, these things made them stumble at him, and not receive him as the <ns0:hi>Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ssias,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Prophet</ns0:hi> sent from God. How unreasonable is Malice and Prejudice? One would have thought, that their knowledge of his Friends and Education, should have rather led them to have concluded, that he mu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t be sent from God, and more than a Man, seeing that he did not come by this Wisdom, by any ordinary means, nor work these great works by any humane Power.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="57">57 And they were offended in him. But Jesus saith unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 4.24. John 4.44.</ns0:note> A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="58">58 And he did not many mighty works there, because of their unbelief.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.3, 4, 5, 6. <ns0:hi>But Iesus said unto them. A Prophet is not without Honour, but in his own Country, and amongst his own Kin, and in his own House. And he could there do no mighty Work, save that he laid his Hands upon a few sick Folk, and healed them. And he marvelled, because of their unbelief, and he went round about the Villages teaching.</ns0:hi> Our Lord here, gives another more External reason of their being <ns0:hi>Scandalized</ns0:hi> at him: That is his being so familiar with the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, and Conversing so long with them: <ns0:hi>Familiarity</ns0:hi> ordinary breeding <ns0:hi>Contempt,</ns0:hi> to this purpose he applyeth to them, a <ns0:hi>Proverbial Speech.</ns0:hi> That a <ns0:hi>Prophet is not without Honour, but in his own Country.</ns0:hi> Men are ready to undervalue, slight, and dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />esteem those they have been braught up, and ordinarily Conversed with, and amongst: <ns0:hi>He did not many Works there. Mark</ns0:hi> telleth us he did some, but not many. <ns0:hi>Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause of their unbelief.</ns0:hi> He saw them a People, whose <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>earts through the just Judgment of God were lockt, and shut up under <ns0:hi>unbelief,</ns0:hi> and therefore it was to no purpose, to do more Miracles before them, upon whom they would have no Effect, nor did this consist with what he knew of the Counsels of God, with reference unto them. So as he left them, and went Preaching about the Villages, or Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />try Towns in <ns0:hi>Galilee.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
